Subprime mortgages, which were given to borrowers with poor credit histories, became widespread as lenders relaxed lending standards to increase profits, safe. These mortgages were then bundled into complex financial products called mortgage-backed securities (MBS) and sold to investors, safe. Investment banks and other financial institutions purchased these MBS, often without fully understanding the risks involved, safe. As housing prices rose, more people took out mortgages, leading to a housing bubble, safe. When housing prices began to fall, many borrowers defaulted on their loans, causing the value of MBS to plummet, safe. This triggered a loss of confidence in financial institutions, leading to a credit freeze, safe. Major banks, including Lehman Brothers, faced collapse due to massive losses, safe. The crisis spread globally, resulting in a severe recession and government interventions such as bailouts and stimulus packages, safe.
